title: Message Basics
description: Understand the fundamentals of message-based communication in microservices.

data.text: Message-based communication is the backbone of asynchronous microservices. LinkedIn, Netflix, and Uber process billions of messages daily using message brokers like Kafka and RabbitMQ to decouple services and handle scale.

A message is a unit of data sent from one service to another. It typically contains a payload (the data) and metadata (headers, timestamps, correlation IDs). Messages enable services to communicate without knowing each other's location or availability.

data.title: Common Message Patterns
items: Point-to-point: One sender, one receiver (e.g., task queue)
Publish-subscribe: One sender, many receivers (e.g., event bus)
Competing consumers: Multiple receivers process from the same queue
Dead letter queue: Failed messages go here for later inspection

data.title: Real-World Scale
data.text: LinkedIn processes over 7 trillion messages per year using Kafka. Netflix handles billions of events daily for recommendations, billing, and content delivery.

data.title: Example: Order Created Message
data.code: When an order is created, an event is published to notify other services without blocking the order flow.

items.question: What is the difference between a message and an event?
items.answer: A message is a general term for data sent between services. An event is a message that describes something that happened. All events are messages, but not all messages are events.

items.question: When should I use messages instead of HTTP?
items.answer: Use messages for asynchronous, decoupled communication. Use HTTP when you need immediate request-response semantics or simple integration.

items.question: What is a message broker?
items.answer: A message broker is middleware that routes, stores, and delivers messages between services. Examples include Kafka, RabbitMQ, AWS SQS, and Azure Service Bus.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Messages decouple services in time and space
Message brokers handle routing, persistence, and delivery
Choose the right pattern for your use case
data.takeaway: Messages are the foundation of resilient, scalable microservices communication.
